document_summary: Justia mirror of N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1, New Jersey's Anti-Eviction Act section listing the good-cause grounds for removing residential tenants statewide.

rules.title: NJ Anti-Eviction Act: grounds for removal of tenants
rules.requirement: A residential tenant may be removed by the Superior Court only on establishing one of the enumerated good-cause grounds (e.g., nonpayment of rent, disorderly conduct, property damage, lease violations, owner retiring the building, condominium conversion, owner occupancy in small buildings).
rules.key_value: Eviction only for statutory good cause (grounds a. through r.)
rules.coverage_conditions: Houses, buildings, mobile homes or land in mobile home parks, or tenements leased for residential purposes.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises with not more than two rental units; hotels, motels or guest houses rented to transient or seasonal tenants; units held in trust for, or permanently occupied by, an immediate family member with a developmental disability.
rules.interaction: Statewide floor; subsection f. requires rent increases to comply with other laws and municipal rent ordinances.
rules.quoted_span: No lessee or tenant or the assigns, under-tenants or legal representatives of such lessee or tenant may be removed by the Superior Court from any house, building, mobile home or land in a mobile home park or tenement leased for residential purposes
rules.extraction_notes: Effective date not stated in the text; the history line (L.1974, c.49, amended through 2013, c.51) is not used to infer one. Document is a Justia mirror of the statute. Relocation-assistance duties are not in this section.
